wars.name: Dutch-Portuguese War (Ceylon)
wars.outcome: The Dutch (allied with Kandy by the treaty of 1638) took the Batticaloa fort on 18 May 1638, Negombo in February 1640, Galle on 13 March 1640 and, after a six-month siege, Colombo in 1656; the Dutch and Portuguese 'divided the occupied areas of Ceylon amicably under a treaty signed in Goa' (undated on the page).
wars.note: The Dutch-Portuguese War article was not opened. 1656 is the last dated fall; Jaffna and the north are undated on both pages. The Kandy page: 'Batticaloa and Trincomalee fell in 1639, Galle in 1640'; the Dutch Ceylon page dates Batticaloa 18 May 1638.

wars.name: Kandyan-Dutch conflict of 1665-1687
wars.outcome: The Dutch seized the ports Kalpitiya, Kottiyar, Batticaloa and Trincomalee and large parts of Sabaragamuwa in 1665; Kandyan campaigns in 1675 and 1684 recaptured some territory.
wars.note: No article opened; a conflict named by this dossier, from one passage of the Kingdom of Kandy page.

wars.name: Kandyan-Dutch war of 1761-1766

zones.text: Matara and Hanwella, the low country

wars.outcome: Kandy annexed Matara and Hanwella in 1761; the Dutch retook them in 1762 and by 1765/1766 forced a treaty returning the border districts and all of Kandy's coastal provinces to the Dutch.
wars.note: No article opened; the Dutch Ceylon page does not mention the war. Year of the treaty: 1765 (text) or 1766 (the 'Treaty of Batticaloa' in the province table).

wars.name: British conquest of Dutch Ceylon
wars.outcome: In February 1795 William V ordered Governor van Angelbeek to place his forces under British protection; Hugh Cleghorn contracted the De Meuron regiment on 30 March 1795; 'After a token resistance, van Angelbeek gave up' and the Dutch surrendered on 14 February 1796. The Kandy page: 'The British rapidly annexed Dutch possessions in Sri Lanka'.
wars.note: The page gives no date for the British capture of Trincomalee and none for the siege of Colombo; Britain was formally ceded the island at Amiens in 1802 (Kandy page).

certainty.note: The Dutch held forts, ports and coastal districts whose inland edge no page opened draws; the only border settlement is the 1765/1766 treaty with Kandy, which the pages name but do not survey.

notes:
Written by sa-06-b on 2026-10-25 from two pages (budget 1-2 for 3 shapes).

CLIOPATRIA SHAPE IS WRONG. The three Dutch Ceylon polygons (1687-1768 with 155 res-5 cells, 1769-1793 and 1794-1795 with 105 cells) are the Kandyan interior: with the gazetteer, every cell of Kandy, Matale, Nuwara Eliya, Badulla and Polonnaruwa district lies inside, most of Anuradhapura, Kurunegala and Monaragala, and nothing of Colombo, Gampaha, Kalutara, Galle, Matara, Jaffna, Mannar, Kilinochchi, Mullaitivu or Vavuniya. The Dutch held the maritime provinces. Cliopatria's British Ceylon (1796-1814, 28,908 km2) has the same bbox and area as the 1769-1795 Dutch polygon, so the British Ceylon dossier probably needs the same correction (the owner of british-ceylon in sa-06 should check). Corrections use a belt of radii around the ports (Jaffna region, Mannar, Puttalam, Negombo, Colombo, Kalutara, Galle, Matara, Trincomalee, Batticaloa), about 53 cells; the inland edge is my reading (pages give none).

NEW KEYFRAMES 1640-1686 and 1796. Cliopatria's row starts in 1687; the page's founding is 13 March 1640. The keyframes for 1640, 1656, 1658 and 1665 are built from the two pages; the 1658 one is confidence 1 (no page dates Jaffna, Mannar, Kalutara or Matara).

DISAGREEMENTS. (1) End of Dutch rule: infobox 16 February 1796, body 14 February 1796 (surrender). (2) The treaty after the 1761 war: 1765 (text) or 1766 (province table, 'Treaty of Batticaloa (1766)'). (3) Governors: the infobox gives Johan van Angelbeek 1794-1796 but the body has him succeed van de Graaf, who resigned after the 1792 orders (a campaign against Kandy planned by van de Graaf and called off). (4) The Dutch Ceylon page dates Batticaloa 18 May 1638; the Kandy page has Batticaloa and Trincomalee falling in 1639.

NOT SETTLED. When the Dutch took Jaffna, Mannar, Kalutara and Matara; whether the Dutch kept Sabaragamuwa after 1675/1684; the districts returned in 1765/1766; the British capture of Trincomalee and the siege of Colombo (both undated on the Dutch Ceylon page); whether the Kandyans got the east coast back in 1796. A gap-filler should open the Dutch-Portuguese War, the Siege of Colombo (1655-56) and the Kandyan war articles if they exist; Treaty of Amiens is on the British Ceylon side.

OTHER STATES. Dutch Coromandel (capital Pulicat), the Dutch holdings on the Indian coast, are a separate entity on the page and not part of this dossier. The Dutch East India Company dossier (dutch-east-india-company) is the governing body: the infobox status is 'Governorate of the Dutch East India Company'. Type colony and family france follow the sibling Dutch colonies and the colours.json note that the Netherlands takes the orange exception inside the france family. Native name 'Zeylan' is from the Kandy page ('Dutch Zeylan'); 'Nederlands Ceylon' is the Dutch form, not read on a page.

GAZETTEER. Mannar, Negombo and Kalutara as places, Hanwella, and the historical region Sabaragamuwa (Ratnapura and Kegalla districts) are not in the gazetteer; coordinates or Ratnapura District stand in for them.


REVIEWER sa-06-b (2026-10-25). Removed kingdom-of-kandy from successors: the February 1796 Madras treaty that would have returned 'much of the eastern coast' was made with the British, the Kingdom of Kandy page says the new king rejected its terms, the kingdom-of-kandy dossier records no 1796 gain, and the 1796 dissolve already passes Trincomalee and Batticaloa to british-ceylon. Added the 1761 loss of Matara and Hanwella (the page says Kandy annexed them) and lowered the 1665 Sabaragamuwa gain to confidence 2.
